But not any ordinary commanders because your astronauts are… cats! Travel into the unknown and send your brave astronauts into space by trying to match your dice rolls with each step of the journey. Do you hop off to explore a planet, or dare to whisker it all by venturing further? MLEM: Space Agency offers exciting decisions and thrilling push your luck experience. With a fun cat in-space theme and Reiner Knizia's trademark strategic depth the game offers a perfect mix of tension, competition and laughter. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Takeoff Phase 3 Travel Phase 4 Crashing 5 Landing Phase 6 Goals 7 Game End Overview Explore space, but make a mark for yourself before you crash! Takeoff Phase Each round starts with a Takeoff Phase. During this phase, each player chooses an astronaut to send on the expedition. Each astronaut grants the player a special effect, so choose wisely! The lead astronaut (Starting Player) is the Commander. Travel Phase The commander of the expedition rolls all dice. The dice have six faces: 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, and afterburner. After they have been rolled, arrange the dice into groups of the same number (e.g. all the 2s). The commander then picks any number of groups whose faces match the rocket marker's current location. For example, at location zero, afterburners, ones, and twos can be used. Threes and fours cannot be used when the rocket is at this location. Each set chosen for movement is added up in its entirety (For example, a set of three 2s has a movement value of 6). The afterburner value is determined by the number of pips on the afterburner symbol at the location. After moving, keep all afterburner dice and unused dice. Discard the rest. If this would result in having no dice left, keep a single die in the pool. Crashing After rolling the dice, if none of them match the allowed dice at the location, a Crash occurs! The Cosmic Failure marker moves on one space. Any astronaut with a parachute MAY disembark (see Landing Phase); all other astronauts are returned to the respective player mats. The Commander is changed to the next player in turn order. The current Expedition ends and there is no Landing Phase. Landing Phase If the Travel phase was a success (did not result in a Crash), the Landing Phase occurs. If the ship is on space 0-5, the landing phase is voided, and a new Travel phase occurs. If the ship is on space 6+, in order of astronauts on the rocket, each player can choose to stay on the ship or disembark. If you choose to disembark at a moon space, place your astronaut on the highest numbered moon linked to that space. If the stop is a moon space and all moons are occupied, you cannot disembark. Each moon accommodates only a single astronaut. If you choose to disembark at a planet space, there are no limitations to the number of astronauts or who controls them. However, the order in which astronauts arrived matters. They will be placed from top to bottom in order of arrival. If the ship manages to reach the last space on the board (deep space), the Commander is placed on the Comet and all passengers are placed on the Galaxy (neither of these places have an occupancy limit). If at any point the Commander disembarks (excluding Deep Space of course), the next astronaut in line takes over as the new Commander. Other astronauts move up a seat in the rocket. Once the Landing Phase is finished, if there are still astronauts in the ship, then commence another Travel Phase. If all Astronauts have disembarked and/or Crashed, the expedition comes to an end and a new one commences with a new Commander. Goals There are four unique goals available to claim as soon as a player meets their condition. Only one player can claim each goal, but a player can claim multiple goals if achieved. Each claimed goal gives 5 points. Fir --- nan

[Rating: 2/10] An OK game that is one of those "look at this theme!" games which is aimed for the demographic that prioritises cuteness over mechanics  I feel more critical on this one than it may deserve, but I am tired of this trend in boardgaming.  Make boardgames appear boring again

[Rating: 2/10] Like Celestia but with creepy cat art. The only anthropomorphic cats I care to tolerate in my games are the ones in Twilight Imperium. Oh, and the ones in the Wing Commander computer games.   Sorry, Mr. Knizia, you may be one of my favorite designers, but this game is a miss for me.

[Rating: 2/10] This game is everything I hate in a box: stupid nonsensical oh-so-quirky animal theme, embarrassing groan worthy puns that the writer is too proud of coming up with, and all that just for a simplistic push your luck dice chucker with little decisions to it. And yet it manages to work for me as a delightfully charming family weight game. [Rating: 3/10] I dont understand how this game is any popular at all. I dont feel like I have any agency at all.

[Rating: 3/10] I'd rather play [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/175117/celestia]Celestia[/url].  Everything about this experience rubbed me the wrong way: the terrible title, flea-bitten theme, and the ticking minutes of my life falling away like despondent tears.  If you lure me back into this litter box, I'll dash for the endgame by hurriedly emptying my cat board. Which I honestly wish were a waterboard, since that would be more fun.

[Rating: 3/10] Knizia crash-lands in this game about placing astronauts with different abilities and rolling dice, hoping that they will end up where they score the most.

[Rating: 3/10] (Played at 2p, 3p, and 5p; probably preferred 3)  I wound up playing a game with all of the advanced stuff added in. What an absolute mess. I probably wouldn't have believed you if you told me Knizia designed this. This is like significantly more complicated Celestia. That isn't something I ever wanted. Slow, long, bloated, flat. I don’t like this kind of bolted-on expansion pack style of variants. There is barely anything to hinge drama on. Give me something like Incan Gold over this any day.

[Rating: 3/10] A push your lucky game where players are taking turns going on a journey to see how far in the galaxy they can go. At any point, players can jump ship to the planet/comet/star/etc. Most points wins the game.

[Rating: 3/10] This push-you-luck game revolves are tokens that you can select before rolling dice. All players can select a token and sometimes these tokens can hurt/help people.  The core game loop is not interesting to me, and the outcome of the game, I feel, typically boils down to luck with just a bit of strategy involving token selection and when to stop rolling.  The theme is bleh. The art is not very good to me. The game loop is meh.  I would not seek this game again.
